# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: "Ruth Fielding at Golden Pass; or, the perils of an artificial avalanche" by Alice B. Emerson (Cupples & Leon, 1925; Gutenberg #76206)

**Main characters**
- Ruth Fielding: heroine, scenario writer/director, orphan raised by Uncle Jabez Potter & Aunt Alvirah Boggs at the Red Mill near Cheslow. Film company: Fielding Film Corporation. Picture "Snowblind" (her 2nd directed film; shot in far North). Later makes "Hearts of the Mountains."
- Tom Cameron: Helen's twin; Ruth's business partner; secretly jealous, in love with Ruth. Calls Ruth "Ruthie"; she calls him "Tommy-boy."
- Helen Cameron: Ruth's chum, Tom's twin; engaged to Chess Copley (who wants to "make his fortune"; uncle backs his "snowball property" deal). Helen is "The Fox"? No—Mary Cox is The Fox.
- Jennie Marchand (née Stone), "Heavy," married to Henri Marchand (Frenchman, in France).
- Ann Hicks, Nettie Parsons, Mercy Curtis (lives in Cheslow), Mary Cox ("The Fox"), Barclay Clayton ("Bark," escort).
- Uncle Jabez Potter: crabbed, complains; Aunt Alvirah: calls Ruth "my pretty."
- Mr. Hammond: president of Alectrion Film Corporation; suggests Ruth act; sends for Edith Lang.
- Layton Boardman: western actor hero, hired from Palatial Films (Sol Bloomberg's company); quarrel with Bloomberg. Injured (sprained ankle, bruised back, head wound) when horse throws him during stampede rescue.
- Viola Callahan: temperamental star hired at high salary; jumps contract to Sol Bloomberg, leaving note with Tony Martano ("Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg"). Earlier seen talking with Bloomberg's agent Charlie Reid in Chicago.
- Dave Sentner (comedian), Shepley (tall thin director, Ruth's right-hand), two cameramen, old deaf trapper character actor, Andy (gangling ranch youth).
- Headwaters Ranch (near Golden Pass, Montana): run by Pa and Ma Gowdy; Ma Gowdy is tall, silent, calico; foreman long lean blue-eyed.
- Edith Lang: crippled ex-actress (WWI Red Cross, leg lost to blood poisoning); coaches Ruth in acting; becomes friend.
- Chess Copley arrives late in book; Helen's engagement.

**Events in order**
1. Ch I: Snowblind premiere at the Palace in Cheslow. Surprise party of Briarwood Hall chums arrives singing "Sweetbriars" song and yell. Party at Ruth's; during Ruth's speech on stage, explosion and fire (film storeroom, mostly smoke).
2. Ch II: Tom rescues Ruth from smoke behind stage; recounts Ruth's backstory (Red Mill, Tom met her in book one, Briarwood Hall, scenario "The Heart of a Schoolgirl").
3. Ch III: Party at hotel; Mr. Hammond arrives; Ruth announces next picture set in Golden Pass, Montana.
4. Ch IV: Hammond says Golden Pass ideal; girls want to come. Layton Boardman's card; Ruth hires him (Tom reluctant to sign).
5. Ch V: Tom objects to Boardman; quarrel over Sol Bloomberg.
6. Ch VI: Helen's news—Chess's uncle backing business; Helen & Chess to marry. Tom takes Ruth driving.
7. Ch VII: Girls stay on; Viola Callahan hired at high salary (Ruth vs Tom quarrel in Ch VIII over salary). Viola reveals romance with Tony Martano; "Jealousy!"
8. Ch VIII: Party at Red Mill; Boardman dances; Tom jealous. Girls depart by train.
9. Ch IX–X: Journey to Chicago. Viola seen talking with Bloomberg's agent Charlie Reid; Ruth/Helen suspicious.
10. Ch XI–XII: Arrival at Golden Pass; Headwaters Ranch. Boardman tames colt; Ruth nearly trampled by stampede of steers; Boardman tries to save her, thrown from horse; Tom and cowboys shoot the steers; Tom says "I couldn't have done anything else."
11. Ch XIII–XIV: Ruth visits Boardman; Tom sees hand-holding and walks off. Rodeo filmed; Helen hit by spent/real bullet (cowboy loaded real cartridges); Ruth and Tom tend her.
12. Ch XV–XVI: Ruth discovers Viola's note (gone to Bloomberg). Hammond arrives, suggests Ruth act.
13. Ch XVII–XVIII: Ruth decides after walk with Tom (jealousy). Camera tests; Boardman praises. Edith Lang sent for.
14. Ch XIX–XX: Edith Lang arrives, coaches Ruth. Tom encounters bear at pool; Ruth finds him; she carries revolver ("cowgirl").
15. Ch XXI–XXII: Avalanche location near deserted cabins. Ruth slips off narrow ledge; Tom climbs down, catches her, lowers her to ledge; Boardman fetches rope, lariat lifts them out. Avalanche scene shot: second unplanned explosion (dynamite house) buries cave company.
16. Ch XXIII–XXV: Tom finds tunnel to light; leads company out; bears in cave; Tom shot in arm (bear clawed); Ruth makes tourniquet with twig. Doctor congratulates Ruth. Chess arrives; Tom and Helen reunited. Boardman confesses he never cares for girls (acting). Hearts of the Mountains premieres in NY; Ruth lifted to stage. Bloomberg's picture (with Viola and Tony) fails. Ending: Helen envies Ruth "and Tom."

**Notable quotes/details**
- Song: "Sweetbriars come here, one by one…"; yell: "S.B.—Ah-h-h! … Briarwood Hall! … That's all!"
- Aunt Alvirah: "It is a good old world, isn't it, Auntie?" / "So it is, my pretty!"
- Tom: "I'm not a friend. I'm only a brother!"
- Viola note text: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg…"
- Picture titles: Snowblind; Hearts of the Mountains (heroine Ann Marks).

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Layton Court Mystery" by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg #72883; first pub. 1926 as "?", Doubleday 1929 edition)

**Dedication**: "To my Father" (author's note on fair-play detective fiction).

**Main characters**
- Roger Sheringham: amateur sleuth, author (~30s), short, stocky, round face, gray eyes, big pipe, Winchester & Oxford; contempt for readers; talks incessantly. Narrator-style prose follows him.
- Alec (Alexander) Grierson: large, broad-shouldered, cheerful; Roger's friend; Oxford cricket (3 years); Scottish (Roger's "Scotch" joke); engaged to Barbara Shannon, then broke it off. Plays the "Watson" to Roger.
- Victor Stanworth: host, ~60, genial, rich, City financier; rented Layton Court (Jacobean, Hertfordshire). Found dead in library, shot through forehead with his revolver, seated in chair behind writing table. Secret blackmailer.
- Lady Stanworth (Lady Cynthia Anglemere, daughter of Earl of Grassingham): Victor's sister-in-law (widow of his younger brother); tall, stately, graying; dislikes Victor. Secretly married to Major Jefferson ~6 months earlier.
- Major Jefferson (Harry): tall, sallow, taciturn ex-army; Stanworth's secretary; ex-officer who forged for a pal; blackmailed by Stanworth; secretly married to Lady Stanworth.
- Graves (Bill Higgins): butler, ex-prize-fighter; Stanworth held something over him.
- Barbara Shannon: 19, small, gray eyes, fair hair; engaged to Alec then broke it off; secretly blackmailed by Stanworth re: her mother.
- Mrs. Shannon: Barbara's mother, doll-like, fussy.
- Mrs. Mary Plant: 26, dark-haired, husband in Soudan Civil Service; blackmailed by Stanworth over pre-marriage matter; paid him; had jewels in safe.
- Inspector Mansfield (Elchester police), Dr. Matthewson, William (gardener, greenfly, "Drat that there Mr. Sheringham!"), Mrs. William (lodge; "cook's brother" gossip), Mary and Alice (maids), Chapman (chauffeur), Mr. Wetherby (Hillcrest Farm), John Prince (farm hand; a red herring, attacked Stanworth once), Albert the landlord (Elchester village pub).

**Events in order**
1. Ch I: 8am, Roger with William in rose garden; meets Alec returning from lodge (posted letter to "bookmaker"). Barbara breaks off engagement with Alec.
2. Ch II: Breakfast; Stanworth's background; Major Jefferson summoned by Graves. Lady Stanworth announces Stanworth missing; library door & windows locked inside; Jefferson & Graves break door; Stanworth dead at desk, revolver, shot in forehead center.
3. Ch III: Library described (French windows, sash window, lattice window, safe—not yet). Typed suicide note "To Whom it May Concern. For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself." Signature with false start "V-i-c." Roger notes Jefferson searching body's pockets; Jefferson sends Roger & Alec away. Mrs. Plant found at safe, claiming jewels.
4. Ch IV: Inspector Mansfield; Dr. Matthewson: died ~2am, one shot. Safe opened later.
5. Ch V: Inspector interview: Jefferson last saw Stanworth ~10pm. Roger & Stanworth in garden. Alec engaged to Barbara (no).
6. Ch VI: Roger's suspicion: Stanworth's shot unnatural (wound center forehead, awkward angle); keys in wrong pocket; Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, butler, Lady Stanworth behaving oddly. Roger decides to investigate with Alec.
7. Ch VII: Blue china vase missing from chimney-piece; ring in dust. Broken fragment found; bullet hole in panel behind pillar = second shot from Stanworth's revolver.
8. Ch VIII–IX: Roger theorizes murder. Alec doubts. Roger finds a folded typed confession with bad signature, theorizes it's a fake; crumpled sheet in waste basket. Lunch; Mrs. Plant leaving at five; Jefferson pleased.
9. Ch X–XI: Roger suspects Mrs. Plant; Alec & Barbara. Safe opened by inspector: documents, £4,000+ cash, Mrs. Plant's jewels. Lady Stanworth's odd behavior.
10. Ch XII–XIII: Search for secret door (none); window fastening trick (handle balance); footprints outside library window (large boots, ~10–11). Someone leaves library; Jefferson's car waiting.
11. Ch XIV–XV: Ash pit: torn pencil fragment: "...that brute Prince... this neighbourhood... serious danger... fright of my life this morning..." Roger suspects John Prince. Mrs. William says Prince attacked Stanworth earlier; works at Hillcrest Farm (Mr. Wetherby). Pub landlord Albert: Prince showed at Elchester Show, back late. Farm visit: bull chase; William (gardener) says a large man came up drive ~8:30pm, later with cook.
12. Ch XVI–XVII: Lecture on Neo-Platonism. Footprints disappeared from bed. Lady Stanworth's face at tea; Mrs. Plant falters. Roger & Alec quarrel over Mrs. Plant. Small vase fragments found in laurels.
13. Ch XVIII–XIX: Handkerchief (scent: Parfum Jasmine, Mrs. Plant's) found in settee cushions; face powder on arm; long fair hair. Mary says cushions tidied before dinner. Dinner bet: Mrs. Plant denies being in library. Roger & Alec plan to search morning room papers.
14. Ch XX–XXI: Roger confronts Mrs. Plant with handkerchief; she says jewels-in-safe story. Roger's midnight search of morning room with Jefferson's permission; discovers Stanworth's blackmail: large cash payments, multiple bank accounts.
15. Ch XXII: Roger's theory: Jefferson killed Stanworth for Mrs. Plant. Alec disagrees ("intuition").
16. Ch XXIII: Inquest (suicide during temporary insanity). Mrs. Plant confesses: Stanworth blackmailed her over pre-marriage matter; she met him 12:30am; he refused; she was in library. She says Jefferson didn't come in. Mrs. Plant received a typed letter from Stanworth (posted from village 8:30am post) saying he'd burnt evidence and would kill himself.
17. Ch XXIV–XXVI: Roger confronts Jefferson; Jefferson: ex-army, forged-check cover-up, Stanworth blackmail. Reveals he and Lady Stanworth secretly married ~6 months ago; he was with her that night. Jefferson: Graves also victim. Roger realizes Stanworth's letter posted after death — proof of fake letter (though Roger later notes the letter couldn't have been posted by Stanworth after death).
18. Ch XXVII: Train to London. Roger's solution: second woman in library = Barbara (hair on settee); murderer = Alec. Roger confronts Alec on train.
19. Ch XXVIII: Alec's confession: he overheard Stanworth blackmail Barbara (re Mrs. Shannon's secret; demand: marry Alec and pay); Alec hid behind curtain; confronted Stanworth; Stanworth fired and missed (vase shattered); Alec twisted wrist and shot him. Alec then burned blackmail papers (~16 envelopes), typed the suicide note, typed letters to Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, Lady Stanworth (and Barbara), smoothed & left footprints, escaped via lattice window using handle trick, reentered via dining room. Roger: "Let's forget." Alec asks whether to tell police; Roger scolds him for being conventional.

**Notes on pipeline/errors**
- Roger's footprint deduction: heel deeper = stepped backwards out.
- Mrs. Plant's letter posted from village by 8:30am post: implies Alec typed & posted it (he went to village at 8am — "bookmaker" lie).
- Dedication/transcriber's notes: corrected typos.
